title: Your passport may be valid and still refused.
subtitle: "Valid until" is not the same as "accepted at check-in". The gap is where voyages end.

title: Many countries require six months' validity beyond your travel dates.
caption: Requirements differ by country and by nationality. Check every country on the itinerary and confirm with the line or your advisor before you pack.
brief: Passport open flat under a desk lamp on a scrubbed table, stamped page catching the light, all personal data illegible.

kicker: Do this at the kitchen table
title: Three documents worth checking today

items.head: The expiry date, in months
items.body: Count forward from your last day ashore, not from the sailing date.

items.head: The name, letter for letter
items.body: The booking must match the passport. A married name added later is the commonest mismatch.

items.head: Blank pages and condition
items.body: Some countries want blank pages, and a torn or water-damaged passport can be refused outright.

title: What travellers assume, and what applies

quote: The document that cancels a trip is rarely the ticket. It is the passport nobody read twice.

text: Photograph every passport page and send them before you pay a deposit.
sub: I check names against the booking, expiry against the final port of the itinerary, and flag anything that needs a renewal window.

title: Save this before your next deposit
body: Send me your itinerary and I'll tell you which countries on it have documentation worth confirming early, and which passports I'd renew now.
